title: The difference of two affine basic sets is a finite disjoint union of affine basic sets
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and write $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V(g_1,\dots,g_n)=\{\mathfrak p:g_1,\dots,g_n\in\mathfrak p\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $B=D(f)\cap V(g_1,\dots,g_r)$ and $C=D(h)\cap V(k_1,\dots,k_s)$ are basic subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, then $B\setminus C$ is a finite pairwise-disjoint union of basic subsets (the empty union is allowed).

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0, proof at line 12049 (the refinement is asserted there); the finite set calculation below is written out from the basic-set description of Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P

proof.text: Define membership of a basic set as simultaneous membership of every g-coordinate in the prime ideal and nonmembership of f; this follows by unfolding toSet and zeroLocus.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (label lemma-constructible, line 5434): the basic sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_m); the set calculation is written out by the agent for the refinement asserted in Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex, proof at line 12049)

proof.text: Induct on s. For s=0, choose the single basic set with g extended by h; its set is exactly the difference, and a singleton family is pairwise disjoint.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (label lemma-constructible, line 5434): the basic sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_m); the set calculation is written out by the agent for the refinement asserted in Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex, proof at line 12049)

proof.text: For the successor step write C_prefix = D(h) ∩ V(k_1,...,k_s) and a = k_(s+1). Apply the induction hypothesis to B \ C_prefix. Construct E = D(fha) ∩ V(g_1,...,g_r,k_1,...,k_s). Since a product is outside a prime ideal exactly when each factor is outside, E = B ∩ C_prefix ∩ D(a). The new second basic set is C_prefix ∩ V(a).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (label lemma-constructible, line 5434): the basic sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_m); the set calculation is written out by the agent for the refinement asserted in Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex, proof at line 12049)

proof.text: Prepend E to the old family. Every old piece lies in B \ C_prefix by the induction union equality, while E lies in C_prefix, so E is disjoint from every old piece. Old pieces remain pairwise disjoint. For each prime, split on membership in C_prefix: outside it the old union is exactly B; inside it the new difference is B ∩ D(a), exactly E. Thus B \ (C_prefix ∩ V(a)) is the union of E and the old family.
